name: Niobium
occurrence: Found combined with tantalum in the mineral columbite-tantalite ('coltan'), a mineral of geopolitical importance for electronics manufacturing.
majorUses: Superconducting magnet wire (MRI machines, particle accelerators)
Jet engine and rocket alloy additives
notableCharacteristics: Was originally named 'columbium' and the two names co-existed for over a century before niobium was internationally standardized in 1949.
whyHere: Its half-filled-adjacent 4d⁴ 5s¹ configuration supports strong metallic bonding, and alloyed with titanium it becomes one of the most practical superconductors — able to carry current with zero resistance at achievable cryogenic temperatures.
didYouKnow: Niobium-titanium alloy wire is the actual superconducting material inside most MRI machines' magnets, carrying enormous current with zero electrical resistance once cooled by liquid helium.
genZNote: Had an identity crisis (columbium vs niobium) for a hundred years. Now quietly runs your MRI's superconducting magnet.
